question: Determine the domain and range of the function $f(x)=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2x}{1+x^2}\right)$ by establishing the required bounds on its argument, and justify that every value in the obtained range is actually attained.
explanation:
Required Condition
The denominator $1+x^2$ is positive for every real $x$. Also,
$$1+x^2-2x=(x-1)^2\geq0$$
Therefore,
$$2x\leq1+x^2$$
and hence
$$\frac{2x}{1+x^2}\leq1$$
Similarly,
$$1+x^2+2x=(x+1)^2\geq0$$
which gives
$$\frac{2x}{1+x^2}\geq-1$$
Thus,
$$-1\leq\frac{2x}{1+x^2}\leq1$$
for every real $x$. Therefore, the domain of $f$ is $\mathbb{R}$.

Verification of the Argument Range
Let
$$t=\frac{2x}{1+x^2}$$
Then
$$tx^2-2x+t=0$$
This quadratic equation has a real solution in $x$ when
$$(-2)^2-4t^2\geq0$$
$$4(1-t^2)\geq0$$
Therefore, every $t\in[-1,1]$ is attained. In particular, $t=1$ occurs at $x=1$, while $t=-1$ occurs at $x=-1$.

Final Result
Since the argument assumes every value in $[-1,1]$ and $\sin^{-1}t$ has range $\left[-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$, the required results are
$$\text{Domain}=\mathbb{R}$$
$$\text{Range}=\left[-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2}\right]$$

options.A: Domain: $[-1,1]$; Range: $\left[-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2}\right]$; both endpoints are attained
options.B: Domain: $\mathbb{R}$; Range: $\left[-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2}\right]$; every value in the range is attained
options.C: Domain: $\mathbb{R}$; Range: $\left(-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2}\right)$; neither endpoint is attained
options.D: Domain: $\mathbb{R}$; Range: $[0,\pi]$; every value in the range is attained
